atoms.name: natural_succ
atoms.rule: a ↑ is a + 1 for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ↑ is a + 1 for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.

atoms.name: natural_pred
atoms.rule: a ↓ is max(0, a - 1) for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ↓ is max(0, a - 1) for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.

atoms.name: is_zero
atoms.rule: a ○ is 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ○ is 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise; negative inputs give NaN.

domain.en: Values are nonnegative integers. A negative input to an atom gives NaN.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms and defaults.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: △₁

operators.name: ◆₂
operators.definition: ◆₂ a = { (☆₂₁ 5) ★₂₃ (☆₂₁ a), if a >= 12; a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12, apply ☆₂₁ to 5, then apply ★₂₃ to the result and (☆₂₁ a); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ♤₃
operators.definition: a ♤₃ b = { 0, if b == 0; a ♥₂₄ (a ♤₃ (b ↓)), if b > 0 and b <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat b times (for b from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): replace the current value by a ♥₂₄ the current value.

operators.name: ★₁₉
operators.definition: a ★₁₉ b = { ◇₄ (◆₁₂ a), if a >= 2 and a < 4 and b < 1; 5, if a < 2 and b >= 1 and b < 2; ◇₄ (▲₁₀ a), else }
operators.plain: If 2 ≤ a < 4 and b < 1, apply ◆₁₂ to a, then apply ◇₄ to the result; otherwise if a < 2 and b ≥ 1 and b < 2, return 5; otherwise apply ▲₁₀ to a, then apply ◇₄ to the result.

operators.name: ♦₂₀
operators.definition: a ♦₂₀ b = { b ★₁₉ b, if a < 1 and b >= 2 and b < 5; ◇₄ (a ★₁₉ a), else }
operators.plain: If a < 1 and b ≥ 2 and b < 5, compute b ★₁₉ b; otherwise apply ★₁₉ to a and a, then apply ◇₄ to the result.

operators.name: ☆₂₁
operators.definition: ☆₂₁ a = { a ↓, if a < 4; ●₁₄ 0, if a >= 10; a ♦₂₀ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 4, subtract one from a, stopping at zero; otherwise if a ≥ 10, apply ●₁₄ to 0; otherwise compute a ♦₂₀ a.

operators.name: ♧₂₂
operators.definition: a ♧₂₂ b = { ☆₂₁ b, if a >= 11 and b >= 0 and b < 1; ☆₂₁ a, if a < 11 and b >= 0 and b < 1; a ★₁₉ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 11 and b ≥ 0 and b < 1, apply ☆₂₁ to b; otherwise if a < 11 and b ≥ 0 and b < 1, apply ☆₂₁ to a; otherwise compute a ★₁₉ a.

operators.name: ★₂₃
operators.definition: a ★₂₃ b = { ♢₉ (◆₁₇ a), if a >= 8 and b >= 10; (◆₁₇ 0) ♦₂₀ (b ○), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 8 and b ≥ 10, apply ◆₁₇ to a, then apply ♢₉ to the result; otherwise apply ◆₁₇ to 0, then apply ♦₂₀ to the result and (1 if b is zero and 0 otherwise).

operators.name: ♥₂₄
operators.definition: a ♥₂₄ b = { a, if a >= 11 and b >= 4 and b < 7; (a ♦₂₀ a) ↓, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 11 and b ≥ 4 and b < 7, return a; otherwise apply ♦₂₀ to a and a, then subtract one from it, stopping at zero.

operators.name: ♣₂₅
operators.definition: ♣₂₅ a = { (▽₈ a) ♥₂₄ (♢₉ a), if a < 2; (◆₁₇ 2) ★₂₃ (▲₁₀ a), else }
operators.plain: If a < 2, apply ▽₈ to a, then apply ♥₂₄ to the result and (♢₉ a); otherwise apply ◆₁₇ to 2, then apply ★₂₃ to the result and (▲₁₀ a).

operators.name: ●₂₆
operators.definition: a ●₂₆ b = { b ◇₁₁, if a < 4 and b < 2; b ★₂₃ a, if a >= 4 and b < 2; b ★₁₉ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 4 and b < 2, apply ◇₁₁ to b; otherwise if a ≥ 4 and b < 2, compute b ★₂₃ a; otherwise compute b ★₁₉ b.

operators.name: ●₂₇
operators.definition: a ●₂₇ = { a ●₂₆ 0, if a >= 5; a ↓, if a >= 0 and a < 3; a ♥₂₄ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 5, compute a ●₂₆ 0; otherwise if 0 ≤ a < 3, subtract one from a, stopping at zero; otherwise compute a ♥₂₄ a.

operators.name: ♧₂₈
operators.definition: a ♧₂₈ b = { (◇₄ b) ★₁₉ (♣₁₈ a), if a >= 6 and b >= 0 and b < 5; (▲₁₀ a) ♥₂₄ (▲₁₀ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 6 and b ≥ 0 and b < 5, apply ◇₄ to b, then apply ★₁₉ to the result and (♣₁₈ a); otherwise apply ▲₁₀ to a, then apply ♥₂₄ to the result and (itself).

operators.name: ▲₂₉
operators.definition: a ▲₂₉ b = { (◆₁₂ b) ★₁₉ (a ◆₁₃), if a >= 12 and b >= 3 and b < 7; a ♧₂₈ (♣₁₈ a), if a >= 12 and b >= 10; (♢₉ b) ♧₂₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 3 and b < 7, apply ◆₁₂ to b, then apply ★₁₉ to the result and (a ◆₁₃); otherwise if a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 10, apply ♧₂₈ to a and (♣₁₈ a); otherwise apply ♢₉ to b, then apply ♧₂₂ to the result and b.

operators.name: ▽₃₀
operators.definition: a ▽₃₀ = { (♣₂₅ a) ●₂₆ (a ↓), if a >= 3 and a < 4; a ♥₂₄ (◇₄ a), if a >= 5; (a ◇₁₁) ◇₁₁, else }
operators.plain: If 3 ≤ a < 4, apply ♣₂₅ to a, then apply ●₂₆ to the result and (a ↓); otherwise if a ≥ 5, apply ♥₂₄ to a and (◇₄ a); otherwise apply ◇₁₁ to a, then apply ◇₁₁ to the result.

operators.name: ♦₃₃
operators.definition: a ♦₃₃ b = { b ♥₂₄ b, if a < 10 and b < 1; b ★₁₉ b, if a >= 10 and b >= 11; a ♧₂₈ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 10 and b < 1, compute b ♥₂₄ b; otherwise if a ≥ 10 and b ≥ 11, compute b ★₁₉ b; otherwise compute a ♧₂₈ b.

operators.name: ▽₄₃
operators.definition: ▽₄₃ a = { a, if a == 0; a ♦₃₃ (▽₄₃ (a ↓)), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then replace r by a ♦₃₃ r.

operators.name: ■₄₄
operators.definition: a ■₄₄ = { 0, if a == 0; a ☆₃₁ ((a ↓) ■₄₄), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then replace r by a ☆₃₁ r.

operators.name: ◇₄₅
operators.definition: a ◇₄₅ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ◇₄₅ (b ↓)) ●₂₇, if b > 0 and b <= 5 }

operators.name: □₄₆

operators.name: ☆₄₇
operators.definition: a ☆₄₇ b = { 0, if a == 0; b ★₁₉ ((a ↓) ☆₄₇ b), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): replace the current value by b ★₁₉ the current value.

operators.name: ★₄₈

operators.name: ♦₆₇
operators.definition: a ♦₆₇ b = { a ▽₆₅, if a >= 7 and b >= 8 and b < 12; 2 ●₅₉, if a >= 0 and a < 7 and b < 8; 6 ♦₃₃ 0, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 7 and b ≥ 8 and b < 12, apply ▽₆₅ to a; otherwise if 0 ≤ a < 7 and b < 8, apply ●₅₉ to 2; otherwise compute 6 ♦₃₃ 0.

operators.name: ■₆₈
operators.definition: a ■₆₈ = { ●₁₄ (a ♦₃₉ a), if a >= 8 and a < 11; ♦₆₄ (a ◆₆₁ 0), if a >= 1 and a < 8; a ♦₆₇ a, else }
operators.plain: If 8 ≤ a < 11, apply ♦₃₉ to a and a, then apply ●₁₄ to the result; otherwise if 1 ≤ a < 8, apply ◆₆₁ to a and 0, then apply ♦₆₄ to the result; otherwise compute a ♦₆₇ a.

operators.name: ♡₆₉
operators.definition: a ♡₆₉ b = { (♣₁₈ 0) ♤₃ a, if a >= 10 and b < 1; (♣₁₈ b) ♧₅₄ (♤₆₃ a), if a < 10 and b >= 1 and b < 5; a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 10 and b < 1, apply ♣₁₈ to 0, then apply ♤₃ to the result and a; otherwise if a < 10 and b ≥ 1 and b < 5, apply ♣₁₈ to b, then apply ♧₅₄ to the result and (♤₆₃ a); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ◆₇₀
operators.definition: a ◆₇₀ = { a ♧₅₇ a, if a >= 4 and a < 5; a ↓, if a >= 9; a ♧₂₈ a, else }
operators.plain: If 4 ≤ a < 5, compute a ♧₅₇ a; otherwise if a ≥ 9, subtract one from a, stopping at zero; otherwise compute a ♧₂₈ a.

operators.name: ♥₇₁
operators.definition: ♥₇₁ a = { a ♤₃ a, if a < 7; ▽₈ a, if a >= 9 and a < 10; a ♧₅₄ a, else }

operators.name: ■₇₅

operators.name: ♣₇₆

operators.name: ♧₉₇
operators.definition: a ♧₉₇ b = { b ♠₁₆, if a < 4 and b >= 10; ♥₇₉ b, if a < 4 and b < 1; ♥₆₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 4 and b ≥ 10, apply ♠₁₆ to b; otherwise if a < 4 and b < 1, apply ♥₇₉ to b; otherwise apply ♥₆₂ to b.

operators.name: ▼₉₈
operators.definition: a ▼₉₈ b = { 4 ♣₉₀ 2, if a >= 5 and b >= 11; a △₇₈ a, if a < 4 and b >= 11; b ♣₃₆, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 5 and b ≥ 11, compute 4 ♣₉₀ 2; otherwise if a < 4 and b ≥ 11, compute a △₇₈ a; otherwise apply ♣₃₆ to b.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ▼₉₉
operators.definition: ▼₉₉ a = { a ♥₈₃, if a >= 3 and a < 8; a ◆₇₂ a, else }
operators.plain: If 3 ≤ a < 8, apply ♥₈₃ to a; otherwise compute a ◆₇₂ a.

operators.name: ★₁₀₀
operators.definition: a ★₁₀₀ = { (a ▽₃₀) ♧₂₂ (♤₆₃ 0), if a >= 2 and a < 3; ◆₁₇ (0 ▼₉₈ a), if a >= 3 and a < 11; (a ♣₉₀ a) ▼₈₈, else }
operators.plain: If 2 ≤ a < 3, apply ▽₃₀ to a, then apply ♧₂₂ to the result and (♤₆₃ 0); otherwise if 3 ≤ a < 11, apply ▼₉₈ to 0 and a, then apply ◆₁₇ to the result; otherwise apply ♣₉₀ to a and a, then apply ▼₈₈ to the result.
